numeral.purpose: Large serif numbers — stat values, countdowns, review scores, greeting text.

body.purpose: General UI text — cards, nav, rows. Times New Roman — a deliberate departure from the technical-HUD sans that preceded it, explicit user direction.

chrome-label.purpose: Structural uppercase labels — eyebrows, card labels, badges.

telemetry.purpose: Live/instrument-style text only — HUD status, transcripts, map labels, errors.

shadows.name: hud-glow-bloom
shadows.value: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(58,214,255,0.55) 0%, rgba(58,214,255,0.28) 35%, transparent 68%); filter: blur(28px)
shadows.purpose: The HUD ring's primary depth cue — luminance, not cast shadow.

shadows.name: active-nav-glow
shadows.purpose: Marks the active nav item, not general elevation.

shadows.name: drawer-shadow
shadows.purpose: The one conventional cast shadow — mobile nav drawer slide-in only.

motion.name: hud-dormant-breathe
motion.purpose: Dormant state — very slow, reads as quietly waiting, not off.

motion.name: hud-pulse-fast
motion.purpose: Speaking state — faster, sharper pulse than listening.

motion.name: hud-dot-illuminate
motion.value: 1.1–1.6s ease-in-out infinite per dot, opacity 0.04→[--dot-amp]→0.04, animation-delay: calc(var(--dot-frac) * duration)
motion.purpose: Each dot in the static wave field animates its own opacity, staggered by angle — the traveling-wave sweep across the ring emerges from every dot lighting itself up in turn, not from an external light source or rotation. Positive delay makes the sweep read clockwise.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default actionable button — navy fill, white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; background: #3b5bdb; color: #fff; padding: 7px 16px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #4a6ae0; }

components.name: Pill Button
components.description: Cyan-outlined pill button — used in Tasks, Settings, Capability Review, Accounts.
components.css: .ds-btn-pill { border: 1px solid #3ad6ff; background: rgba(34, 211, 238, 0.12); color: #4dcabc; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 999px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-pill:disabled { opacity: 0.55; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Standard content card — current flat convention, superseded going forward by a glass treatment.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #161b27; border: 1px solid rgba(60, 80, 130, 0.3); border-radius: 10px; padding: 18px 20px; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: rgba(80, 110, 170, 0.5); } .ds-card-label { font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #5a6e96; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; color: #f0f2f8; }

components.name: Cyan Badge
components.description: Status/tag badge in the teal-cyan accent.
components.css: .ds-badge-cyan { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.03em; background: rgba(77, 202, 188, 0.1); color: #4dcabc; border: 1px solid rgba(77, 202, 188, 0.25); }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Sidebar navigation item, default and active states.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 7px 8px; border-radius: 6px; color: #8898b8; text-decoration: none; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 450; transition: all 0.15s; cursor: pointer; border: none; background: none; width: 100%; text-align: left; } .ds-nav-item:hover { color: #f0f2f8; background: rgba(59, 91, 219, 0.12); } .ds-nav-item-active { color: #f0f2f8; background: rgba(59, 91, 219, 0.2); border-left: 2px solid #3ad6ff; padding-left: 6px; box-shadow: -1px 0 8px rgba(58, 214, 255, 0.25); }

components.name: HUD Ring (signature)
components.description: The system's signature status indicator — no drawn ring lines anymore. A dense static field of dots fills an annulus around the NORTH wordmark (an invisible outer boundary, no stroke), each dot self-illuminating with a staggered delay so a traveling wave of light sweeps clockwise across the fixed field. Color is state-driven: cyan while transcribing, teal while processing/thinking, red on error.
components.css: .ds-hud-ring { position: relative; width: 160px; height: 160px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-hud-glow { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(58,214,255,0.55) 0%, rgba(58,214,255,0.28) 35%, transparent 68%); filter: blur(28px); opacity: 0.42; } .ds-hud-glow-core { position: absolute; width: 40%; height: 40%; top: 30%; left: 30%; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(255,255,255,0.9) 0%, #3ad6ff 30%, transparent 72%); filter: blur(10px); opacity: 0.32; } .ds-hud-dot { fill: #3ad6ff; opacity: 0.04; animation: ds-dot-illuminate 1.6s ease-in-out infinite; animation-delay: calc(var(--dot-frac) * 1.6s); } @keyframes ds-dot-illuminate { 0%, 82% { opacity: 0.04; } 90% { opacity: var(--dot-amp, 1); } 100% { opacity: 0.04; } }

narrative.overview:
North is a single-operator instrument panel, not a product being sold to anyone. Every surface is built for exactly one person (Nishad) who already knows the system intimately — so the aesthetic optimizes for a HUD an expert operator glances at and trusts, not a landing page persuading a stranger. The register is JARVIS: dry, direct, technical, confident. Density and precision read as competence, not as clutter to soften.

The system already carries a real, deliberately-built identity: a glowing cyan signal ring as its signature HUD element (now expressed as a self-illuminating dot field, not drawn ring lines), a dark navy-grounded base with a faint repeating grid texture behind all chrome, and a type pairing that splits duties cleanly. This is refinement territory, not a blank canvas.

North should never read as a generic SaaS dashboard. No purple-to-blue gradients, no cards nested in cards, no rounded-square icon tiles stacked above headings.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, navy-grounded base with a faint cyan grid texture behind every chrome surface — never a flat, textureless background.
One signature circular HUD element — a self-illuminating dot field, no drawn ring lines — carries the system's entire emotional range through which dots light up, how fast, and in what color.
Two labeling registers, used deliberately: Times New Roman uppercase for structural chrome, JetBrains Mono uppercase for live telemetry only.
Cyan and navy-blue are the informational/interactive defaults; warm gold is reserved for one specific content category; red is reserved for genuine errors.

rules.name: The Signal-vs-Action Rule
rules.body: HUD Signal Cyan means the system is telling you something. Navy Interactive Blue means you can act on this. Don't swap their roles.

rules.name: The One Gold Rule
rules.body: Warm Gold is reserved for the long-horizon goal category. It does not become a general secondary accent elsewhere.

rules.name: The Two Labels Rule
rules.body: Chrome Label (Times New Roman) names static UI structure. Telemetry (JetBrains Mono) names something genuinely live or system-reported right now.

rules.name: The Glow-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth in this system comes from luminance far more than cast shadow. Reach for a glow treatment before box-shadow.

dos: Do use HUD Signal Cyan for anything reporting live system state or telemetry; use Navy Interactive Blue for anything actionable.
Do build new panels and cards glass-first — low-opacity fill, backdrop blur, glowing border (but never on a circular element — see Don'ts).
Do use JetBrains Mono only for genuinely live/telemetry text.
Do keep the grid-texture + gradient-vignette background on every chrome surface.
Do express component state through glow, opacity, color, and motion on existing shapes before reaching for a new icon or shape.
Do set appearance: none on any custom-styled <button> up front, not just override its colors.
donts: Don't introduce a purple-to-blue gradient, nested cards, or rounded-square icon tiles above headings.
Don't introduce a third cyan shade.
Don't use Warm Gold as a general secondary accent.
Don't add a third button shape — reconcile the existing rectangular and pill systems first.
Don't attempt floating 3D wireframe holograms or literal dated browser-chrome styling — both out of scope for a 2D web app.
Don't ship new nv-input/nv-textarea/nv-button usage without first fixing the missing --cyan-500, --cyan-300, and --border-subtle custom properties.
Don't put backdrop-filter: blur() on a circular element — the blur clips hard to the border-radius and shows up as a visible gray/black circular edge (confirmed live bug).
Don't rely on background/border overrides alone to hide a <button>'s native chrome — appearance: none is required (confirmed live bug).
